page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, comprising 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall into the bottom 25%, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute scaling. The tradeoff is lower processing throughput, as evidenced by weak scores in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. This instance is best suited for workloads such as small-scale databases, caching layers, memory-bound data processing, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw CPU performance.
